title: Budgeted Replanning for Embodied Agents
titleZh: BRACE：面向具身智能体的预算化重规划
authors: Shuaijun Liu, Feiyang You, Xingwei Chen, Ningxin Su
short_description: BRACE treats replanning as a budgeted control loop for embodied agents, deciding when to replan, which mode to use, and how many tokens and milliseconds each replanning call can spend. Together with E-RECAP, it reduces replanning token counts and latency SLO violations while preserving task success across navigation, manipulation, coordination, and AirSim benchmarks.
shortDescriptionZh: BRACE 将具身智能体的重规划建模为预算化控制循环，决定何时重规划、采用何种模式，以及每次重规划调用可以使用多少 token 和延迟预算。结合 E-RECAP 后，该方法在导航、操作、协作和 AirSim 场景中降低重规划 token 开销与延迟 SLO 违约率，同时保持任务成功率。

sections.title: Overview
sections.text: Embodied agents frequently replan to recover from execution drift, partial observability, and coordination hazards, but repeated LLM-based replanning can accumulate long textual contexts and produce heavy-tailed latency. BRACE reframes replanning as a budgeted systems primitive with explicit per-call token budgets and latency service-level objectives.

sections.title: Method
sections.text: BRACE decides whether replanning should occur, selects a replanning mode, and allocates a token budget and latency SLO for each call. Its reusable efficiency module, E-RECAP, progressively prunes replanning contexts across transformer layers while preserving task-critical head and tail tokens.

sections.title: Results
sections.text: Across Meta Habitat, RoboFactory, and AirSim, BRACE with E-RECAP substantially reduces replanning-call token counts and SLO violations. In harder RoboFactory settings where open-loop, frozen-plan, and No BRACE baselines fail, BRACE + E-RECAP recovers task success while reducing deadline misses.
